body.statement: Whenever \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed dimensions, \(\alpha\), and the stated bounded class constants, such that for every \(T_0,T_1\) and every nonempty margin stratum, \(c\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\le R_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\le\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)}\mathbb E_\vartheta[\operatorname{diam}_2\{\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}\}]\le C\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\). The lower bound is obtained from legal pairs in the original full-panel Gaussian experiment, including constant-post-factor compensated loading rotations, direct post-noise pairs, and bounded-signal saturation pairs.
body.justification: This is the first sharp expected-diameter frontier for a full sparse causal-effect vector when the decoding operator is learned from the same panel.
body.gap: NicklVanDeGeer2013 characterizes sparse-vector honesty with an observed regression design; it does not contain the pre-panel loading-rotation channel or the \(\kappa_s(L)\)-indexed bounded-signal frontier.
body.consumer: It quantifies the shortest globally valid full-vector uncertainty achievable in the fixed-factor analyses of HeLiShiMiao2026.
